title: CV. Stephen J Newhouse
text:
Experience

Head of Professional Services & Senior Bioinformatician · Biorelate Ltd.
June 2021 – present · United Kingdom (Manchester)

Built and lead the Professional Services team at Biorelate. I set the strategy, hire the team, and own client outcomes.
Run client onboarding, training, and product trials. Make sure people actually use what we ship and get real value out of it.
Lead bespoke consultancy engagements, applying Biorelate’s NLP, knowledge graph, and biomedical AI stack to whatever the client’s actual problem is.
Help close deals. I work alongside Sales and Business Development on technical scoping, demos, and discovery.
Sit between Product and clients. The PS team is one of Product’s loudest internal voices on what’s working and what isn’t.

Selected achievements

Built the Professional Services function from zero. Consistent client satisfaction and renewals to date.
Contributed to over £1M in annual sales.
Built strong working relationships across Sales, Business Development, Marketing, Product, and Data Science.



Data Scientist · Grid Edge
January 2021 – June 2021 · United Kingdom

Worked with the data-science team on ML products. Delivered on time, on budget, on spec.
Built ML models for multivariate time-series forecasting that worked when clients only had a small amount of data to train on.
Key achievement: built an EDA and ML web application in Streamlit (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, PyCaret, Prophet, MLflow, Docker) so the team could explore, clean, and track time-series experiments without leaving the browser.



Chief Technology Officer (interim, head-hunted) · Mindwave Ventures (now Claryon Systems)
August 2019 – February 2020 · London, UK · UK & India
Head-hunted by the CEO to take a CTO-level role spanning Mindwave’s UK and India engineering teams during the rebrand to Claryon Systems. NHS-focused digital-health delivery.

Ran and mentored a development team in India. Set engineering standards, established code-review practice, and a regular working rhythm with the UK product and delivery side.
Worked with NHS stakeholders and the UK team to turn clinical and operational requirements into architectures, backlogs, and implementation plans the engineering team could ship against.
Led containerisation and Docker security for NHS-facing platforms: secure network design, container hardening, and deployment pipelines fit for UK healthcare security expectations.
Tightened communication between UK client-facing colleagues and the engineering team in India. Less requirements ambiguity, faster delivery on NHS and related digital-health work.



King’s College London · (8 years total, 2011 – 2019)

Bioinformatics Module Lead, Genomic Medicine MSc
November 2015 – August 2019 · KCL & SGUL
Designed and ran the bioinformatics week for the MSc in Genomic Medicine: lectures and hands-on practicals tied to the 100,000 Genomes Project. Course material: snewhouse/Genomic-Medicine-MSc-Bioinformatics.


Data Science Group Lead, Department of Biostatistics & Health Informatics
November 2015 – August 2019 · London, UK

Led a sub-team working on genomic and transcriptomic data for neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders.
Built bioinformatics pipelines for genomic and transcriptomic analysis, including drug-repurposing pipelines using public and private datasets.
Ran a small Core Bioinformatics service that took Illumina SNP and expression-array data from raw output to analysis-ready.
Sat on the Bioinformatics and IT Committee for the South London Genomic Medicine Centre.
Consulted on NGS pipelines for local NHS Genetics Labs and research groups.
Consulted across the department on biostatistics, statistical genetics, ML, predictive modelling, and EDA.
Co-supervised PhD students (academic and pastoral support).
Taught BSc, MSc, PhD, NHS, and working-professional cohorts.



Senior Bioinformatician, NIHR BRC for Mental Health, Institute of Psychiatry
September 2011 – August 2019 · London, UK
The umbrella post for the KCL years above. Bioinformatics support and methods development for psychiatric and neurodegenerative research across the BRC, including the SGDP affiliation below.


Associate Member, MRC SGDP, Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience
March 2015 – August 2019 · London, UK

title: About
text:
I’m Dr Stephen J Newhouse: BSc (Hons), MSc, PhD. 20+ years in bioinformatics, genomics, and life-sciences data science, working across academia, the NHS, and industry.
I’m currently Head of Professional Services and Senior Bioinformatician at Biorelate Ltd. in Manchester, UK. I lead the team that turns Biorelate’s biomedical AI, knowledge graph, and NLP products into real client outcomes in target, drug, and biomarker discovery, indication expansion, and systems biology.
Before Biorelate I held roles at Grid Edge (Data Scientist), Mindwave Ventures (CTO), and UCL (Honorary Senior Lecturer). I spent eight years at King’s College London as a Senior Bioinformatician and Data Science Group Lead at the NIHR Biomedical Research Centre for Mental Health, including module-leading the Bioinformatics module of the MSc in Genomic Medicine. Earlier postdoctoral work at the Institute of Psychiatry, University of Cambridge, and Queen Mary University of London, where I also did my PhD in Genetics.

title: Dr Stephen J Newhouse
text:
I’ve spent 20+ years in bioinformatics, genomics, and life-sciences data science. That sounds like a long time until you remember how much the field has changed in just the last five. The questions stay the same though: how do we make sense of complex biomedical data, and how do we turn it into something that actually helps people?
At Biorelate I lead Professional Services. In practice that means making sure the science we’re doing connects to what our clients actually need: accelerating a drug-discovery pipeline, untangling a messy real-world data workflow, or helping a team understand what they’ve got and what they can do with it.
Before this I worked across academia, the NHS, and pharma, building and leading teams, shipping ML models, and trying to make large-scale data projects land well in the real world.
Somewhere along the way I appear to have become an Agentic Engineer. Not by design, more by osmosis and a stubborn refusal to fall behind the LLM Joneses. Right now I’m particularly interested in where knowledge graphs, RAG, and multi-omics data are heading, and what that means for personalised medicine.






Always happy to connect with people working at the intersection of data, biology, and drug discovery. → LinkedIn · Email

title: Welcome. Site relaunch.
text:
After several years untouched, this site is back online: rebuilt with Quarto, tidied up, and pointed firmly at where I’m spending my time now: agentic AI alongside the bioinformatics and ML for health work.
A few practical notes:

The old 2018-era homepage, CVs, and workshop materials are preserved under /archive/. Links you may have shared still work.
The Projects page is where new work will land.
This is the first post on the new Blog. Expect short, technical notes on what I’ve learned, broken, and fixed.

If you’d like to chat about work, collaboration, or just say hi, LinkedIn is the fastest way to reach me.

title: aa-ma-forge
text:
aa-ma-forge (AA-MA: Advanced Agentic Memory Architecture) is an in-progress framework for giving LLM agents structured, persistent, queryable memory, beyond a vector store.
The goal: agents that genuinely accumulate knowledge across sessions, with clean separation between episodic, semantic, and procedural memory.

title: aa-ma-forge
text:
Why it matters
Most “agent memory” today is just RAG with extra steps. Real agentic systems need memory that supports recall, consolidation, forgetting, and reasoning over what was learned.
→ Repository on GitHub
